title: Effectiveness of Generate–Validate–Repair (GVR) with Deterministic Validation vs LLM-only for Reducing Unsafe Network Changes
research_question: Does an automated generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline that uses a deterministic network validator materially reduce the incidence of unsafe or semantically incorrect network changes relative to an LLM-only generation pipeline on a curated NetOps task bank?
confirmatory_hypotheses: A closed-loop generate–validate–repair pipeline incorporating a deterministic validator reduces the post-application unsafe-change incidence by at least 50% (relative reduction) compared to LLM-only generation on the same tasks (paired design).
exploratory_questions: What fraction of GVR-corrected cases introduce new, validator-undetected failure modes (GVR-introduced failures)?
How many repair iterations are required on average for successful repairs, and what is the average model-call cost per successful repair?
How sensitive are results to validator choice (primary validator vs independent secondary validator) and to task cluster (topology class)?
benchmark_scope: Curated public/synthetic NetOps task bank (200 confirmatory tasks) covering four topology clusters: enterprise, campus, datacenter, and edge (50 tasks each). Tasks are intent→configuration translation problems synthesised from public config corpora and canonicalized into machine-checkable intents.
primary_estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (proportion of tasks that transition from unsafe under LLM-only to safe under GVR, reported as absolute and relative reduction; computed by paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor using exact McNemar test).
secondary_estimands: Average repair iterations per repaired task (mean, 95% CI).
Proportion of tasks where GVR introduced a new validator-detected failure (GVR-introduced-failure rate).
Model-call cost per successful repair (mean, 95% CI).
sampling_plan: Confirmatory sample: 200 tasks total (4 topology clusters × 50 tasks each). For each task: generate a single deterministic initial LLM output (temperature=0, one API call, stored). Paired conditions use the same initial output: (A) LLM-only — apply initial generated config to primary deterministic validator (Batfish) and record pass/fail; (B) GVR — run the same initial LLM output through the deterministic validator; if validator reports violations, issue one automated repair prompt to the same LLM (maximum 1 repair call per task per registered adapter contract) and re-validate; apply final repaired config to emulator/validator and record pass/fail. Task ordering randomized with fixed seed. Inclusion/exclusion: tasks with infrastructure execution failures are logged and handled per missingness plan. Planned model-calls: initial 200 calls + up to 200 repair calls = maximum 400 model calls (adapter-enforced cap).
power_and_precision_plan: Primary confirmatory analysis: exact McNemar test (two-sided, alpha=0.05) on paired binary outcomes (LLM-only pass/fail vs GVR pass/fail), executed by paired_binary_analysis_v1. Report absolute risk reduction, relative reduction, exact p-value, and 95% confidence intervals for paired difference using exact/pivot methods. Planning assumptions: baseline unsafe-change incidence ≈30%; target effect = 50% relative reduction (e.g., 30%→15% absolute reduction 0.15). With n=200, power ≈0.8 under these assumptions; sensitivity analyses re-evaluate power under baseline rates 20% and 40%. Secondary estimands use descriptive CIs and exploratory regressions (see multiplicity_plan).
exclusion_rules: Pairs where neither condition completes due to infrastructure execution failures are excluded from primary analysis and logged as technical failures.
Pairs with primary validator vs emulator disagreement are flagged and excluded from primary analysis per contamination_plan (deterministic rule).
missingness_plan: Execution-infrastructure failures: pairs where neither condition completes are excluded from primary analysis and counted in a technical-failure log. Single-condition technical failures follow the paired_binary_analysis_v1 failed_call_treatment 'complete_pair_primary' (documented in the execution manifest). All exclusion/handling decisions are deterministic and logged. Sensitivity analysis: run 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' to assess robustness.
analysis_plan: Primary confirmatory analysis executed by paired_binary_analysis_v1. Primary test: exact McNemar test (two-sided, alpha=0.05) on paired binary outcomes. Report absolute and relative reductions, exact p-value, and 95% CI. Secondary/exploratory analyses: (a) logistic regression (repair_success ~ topology_cluster + initial_validator_failure_type + repair_iterations) on confirmatory sample (exploratory; report unadjusted p-values and effect sizes); (b) descriptive statistics for repair-iteration counts and model-call costs. All inputs, seeds, model-call logs, validator diagnostics, and hashes recorded and published in execution manifest. Sensitivity analyses per power_plan and missingness_plan will be executed programmatically.
multiplicity_plan: One pre-registered primary confirmatory test (McNemar). All secondary tests are explicitly labeled exploratory. For multiple secondary comparisons, apply Bonferroni or Benjamini–Hochberg correction as appropriate; exploratory subgroup claims reported with unadjusted p-values and explicitly flagged as exploratory.
contamination_plan: Benchmark: Public/synthetic NetOps task bank v1. Risk factors: validator coverage blind spots leading to overfitting of repairs; GVR introducing new failure modes not captured by primary validator; model API outages causing incomplete pairs. Detection: primary deterministic validator (Batfish) on every generated/repaired config; secondary validator: Mininet data-plane emulator + reachability test-suite on randomized 10% holdout (fixed seed). Automated discrepancy detector flags any Batfish vs Mininet disagreement. Item-flagging: flag if Batfish verdict != Mininet verdict; flag if GVR requires repair and final validator reports warnings or non-pass; flag if repair attempt reaches maximum allowed attempts without pass. Analysis treatment: primary analysis excludes tasks flagged for validator-emulator disagreement (conservative predetermined treatment). Sensitivity analyses: (a) include flagged tasks as failures for GVR; (b) include flagged tasks as successes for GVR; (c) report results restricted to unflagged subset. All handling deterministic and logged. Residual uncertainty: validators may jointly miss real operational failures not modelled.
stopping_rule: Stop when all tasks in the confirmatory sample (n=200) have been processed or when the adapter-enforced maximum model-call cap is reached (maximum_model_calls=400). Per-task limits: initial generation 1 call; if validator fails, allow at most 1 repair call (per registered adapter contract). Any technical runtime failures are handled per missingness_plan and logged; no post-hoc repeats outside the frozen retry policy.
planned_outputs: Execution manifest and raw experiment artifacts (model-call logs, validator outputs, emulator traces, hashes).
Statistical-results file with primary and secondary analyses and sensitivity analyses.
Evidence-to-claim table and nearest-work comparison matrix.
Complete IEEE LaTeX manuscript (≤5 pages) including mandatory Disclosure Statement.
